inputs.prompt: Studio product photograph, soft daylight, shallow depth of field, realistic materials, sharp focus on the keys. A handheld TV remote built like a small mechanical keyboard macropad. A slim conventional bar-shaped remote in matte charcoal 3D-printed plastic with visible fine print layer lines, cream keycaps, lying on a light oak coffee table next to a TV in the background. Its ten keys sit in a regular grid of three columns: Back, Up, Home on the top row; Left, OK, Right on the second row; A, Down, B on the third row; and a single Play/Pause key centred on the fourth row. Every key is an identical separate square low-profile mechanical keyboard keycap, exactly like the keys of a Kailh Choc low-profile keyboard: a thin flat square cap about 18 mm wide, standing a few millimetres above a flat switch plate on its own visible low-profile switch, with even gaps between keys and a small printed legend on each cap.
